diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$.
However, to the best of our knowledge, sufficient conditions to guarantee the uniqueness of the fixed-point of~$G$ for non-parametric $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ is still an open problem.

We perform a rigorous convergence analysis of our algorithm to show that it converges to the true $\CW_2$-barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ in an almost sure sense (see Setting~\ref{sett: convergence} and Theorem~\ref{thm: fixedpoint-convergence}).

issues.failure_explanation: The prose advertises unconditional almost-sure convergence to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter. What the paper proves unconditionally (Theorem thm: fixedpoint-convergence statement (i)) is precompactness of (widehat mu_t) with every accumulation point a fixed point of G; identifying the limit with the barycenter is established only conditionally on G having a unique fixed point (statement (ii)), a condition the paper itself states is open for non-parametric inputs. Since fixed points of G need not coincide with the (unique) barycenter when several fixed points exist, the unconditional barycenter-convergence claim is not supported by the formal content.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the abstract and Introduction contribution (ii) with the uniqueness condition, e.g., 'provably convergent to a fixed point of G, which coincides with the 2-Wasserstein barycenter when G has a unique fixed point'. No mathematical repair is needed because the formal results are correctly stated.
issues.overall_effect: Readers of the abstract and contribution (ii) may take away an unconditional barycenter-convergence guarantee that the theorems do not deliver; the formal statements (thm: fixedpoint-convergence and cor: fixedpoint-convergence-entropic) are themselves precisely conditional and remain valid.
issues.title: Abstract and Introduction claim unconditional almost-sure convergence to the barycenter, omitting the unique-fixed-point hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem statements are correct and explicitly conditional; only the summary prose omits the hypothesis. A one-sentence qualification repairs it with no loss of mathematical content, rates, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem: truncation-choice supplies the thresholds overline{r}_1, overline{r}_2 only as existential functions of (rho, epsilon) (and (rho, nu_1,...,nu_K, epsilon)) with no Borel-measurability requirement, in contrast to the estimator thresholds overline{n}, tilde{theta} in Assumption asp: OTmap-estimator (iii), which are explicitly required to have Borel dependence. Setting sett: convergence then defines R-hat_t from these thresholds evaluated at the random overline{rho}_t and asserts R-hat_t is CF_t-measurable; the proof of Theorem thm: fixedpoint-convergence applies the lemma at the random overline{rho}_t and takes conditional expectations given CF_t, which requires the thresholds to be Borel functions of overline{rho}_t. An arbitrary non-measurable choice of overline{r}_1, overline{r}_2 would break the adaptedness claim and every conditional-expectation bound that drives the convergence argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define overline{r}_1(rho, epsilon) and overline{r}_2(rho, nu_1,...,nu_K, epsilon) canonically as the minimal r satisfying the deterministic bounds derived in the proof of Lemma lem: truncation-choice (these bounds are Borel in rho), or add an explicit Borel-dependence requirement on overline{r}_1, overline{r}_2 parallel to that on overline{n}, tilde{theta} in Assumption asp: OTmap-estimator (iii); the measurability note in Setting sett: convergence then holds and all conditional-expectation steps go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The adaptedness of (R-hat_t) and the conditional-expectation error bounds (eqns fixedpoint-convergence-proof-approx, -pushforward-k, -pushforward, -estimator) underlying Theorem thm: fixedpoint-convergence, and hence the entropic-estimator corollary cor: fixedpoint-convergence-entropic, are unsupported as written. The convergence conclusions themselves are unaffected once measurable thresholds are chosen.
issues.title: Measurability of the truncation thresholds r-bar_1, r-bar_2 is never established, leaving the adaptedness of R-hat_t and the conditional-expectation bounds unsupported
issues.why_classification: The gap is a missing standard measurability hypothesis, not a failed argument: a canonical minimal-threshold (measurable-selection) definition or an added Borel-dependence clause repairs it locally, with no change to any conclusion, rate, or advertised scope.
